sentences.text: This Misc. Appeal has been filed by appellant-Insurance Company under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, challenging the Award dated 25th January 2016 passed by Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Sheopur, in Claim Case No. 01 of 2015.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT), Sheopur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Challenging the impugned Award, the appellant seeks exoneration from its liability to pay the compensation amount on the ground that the document presented by claimants, purported to be Temporary Permit receipt (01470639 R/10) for the offending vehicle, was found to be forged.
Upon verification, it was determined that the permit related to a different vehicle (RJ 25 GA 0672), and not the offending vehicle (RJ GA 0678), thus, the Insurance Company should not be held liable.
The appellant was not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4805 2 MA-396-2016 provided adequate opportunity to substantiate its defence regarding the forged document, which is a grave legal error.

The driving licence of the vehicle driver was not valid at the time of the accident,
constituting a breach of the insurance policy terms, further exonerating the Insurance Company from liability.

sentences.text: Along with the appeal, the appellant has filed an application i.e. IA No. 1889 of 2016 under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Civil Procedure Code (CPC) seeking permission to introduce additional evidence.
The appellant has presented a verification of Temporary Permit (Receipt No.01470639 R/10) issued by the District Transport Officer, Sawai Madhopur, dated 29th March 2016.
The document was not available to the appellant at the time of passing the impugned award and is now being submitted for a just disposal of the case.

4. Learned Counsel for respondents No.7 and 8 opposed appeal and contended that the Insurance Company's liability should remain as determined in the impugned award, and objected to the introduction of additional evidence at this stage.

5. After hearing the parties and perusing the record, this Court finds that the Claims Tribunal did not afford the appellant adequate opportunity to substantiate its case regarding the forged Temporary Permit and breach of policy terms.
Therefore, the matter deserves to be and is hereby remanded to learned Claims Tribunal to reconsider the issue of liability afresh, in light of the additional evidence presented by the appellant.
The Claims Tribunal shall pass a fresh award after hearing both parties only the point of liability .

Both NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4805 3 MA-396-2016 parties are directed to appear before the Claims Tribunal on 20th February 2026.
6. With the aforesaid, the instant misc. appeal stands disposed of.
